items.stem: Why does a human activity in one place often affect many parts of an ecosystem?

options.text: Because ecosystems have no living parts
Because an ecosystem is a system of connected parts
Because each species lives completely on its own
Because humans live outside of all ecosystems

items.explanation: An ecosystem is a system of connected parts, so a change in one part can ripple out to the others.

options.text: Air pollution from factories
A kind of renewable energy
A natural predator of fish
Water that flows over land and carries materials into bodies of water

items.explanation: Runoff is water that flows over the land and carries soil, fertilizer, or other materials into rivers, lakes, and oceans.

items.stem: In the green lake, why did the fish die after the algae bloom?

options.text: The algae used up the oxygen in the water
The algae ate the fish directly
The water became too cold for fish
The fish were caught by people

items.explanation: As the algae died and broke down, bacteria used up the oxygen in the water, so the fish could no longer breathe.

items.stem: Which of these is an example of habitat loss?

options.text: Adding solar panels to a roof
Recycling glass and paper
Clearing a forest to build houses
Planting a community garden

items.explanation: Habitat loss happens when the natural place a species lives is destroyed, such as clearing a forest for development.

items.stem: Why can an invasive species spread so easily in a new ecosystem?

options.text: It always eats only plants
It often has no natural predators there
It makes the soil richer for native plants
It cannot reproduce in the new area

items.explanation: With no natural predators in its new home, an invasive species can multiply quickly and crowd out native species.

options.text: Companies that sell wild animals
Rules that ban all fishing
Machines that clean rivers
Benefits healthy ecosystems give people, like clean water and air

items.explanation: Ecosystem services are the benefits people get from healthy ecosystems, such as clean water, clean air, food, and fertile soil.

items.stem: Which of these is a renewable resource?

options.text: Sunlight
Coal
Oil
Natural gas

items.explanation: Sunlight is renewable because nature replaces it constantly. Coal, oil, and natural gas are nonrenewable.

items.stem: A farmer reduces how much fertilizer washes into a nearby lake. What is the most likely result?

options.text: The lake immediately loses all its fish
The lake's water turns green faster
The lake has fewer algae blooms and can recover
The lake gains an invasive species

items.explanation: Less fertilizer runoff means fewer nutrients feeding algae, so blooms are less likely and the lake can begin to recover.

items.stem: Which choice best shows conservation in action?

options.text: Draining a wetland for a parking lot
Setting aside a protected area to keep a habitat whole
Releasing a new species into a lake
Dumping extra waste into a river

items.explanation: Conservation is the protection and careful use of ecosystems, such as setting aside protected areas to keep habitats whole.

items.stem: What is the best summary of how humans affect Earth's systems?

options.text: Humans can only harm ecosystems, never help them
Humans have no real effect on ecosystems
Human effects always stay in one small place
Human activities can both disrupt and help maintain ecosystems

items.explanation: Human activities can disrupt ecosystems through pollution and habitat loss, but human choices can also protect and restore them.
